title: Beyond Bolted-On Screen Readers: Narrative Phenomenology, the RNIB Roundhouse Sensory Dark, and Perceptual-Cognitive Unity (Rasa-Darśan)
author: Borealis Serenity Hedling
acknowledgement: Inspired by research-projection experiments pioneered by Flyxion (@standardgalactic).
limitations: Browser speechSynthesis voices lack the emotional warmth and breath cadence of a human narrator.
Replacing 2D spatial movement with discrete gestures trades open-world exploration freedom for narrative coherence.

turns.speaker: Speaker A
turns.text: Imagine entering a darkened room with no visual screen at all. Instead of a robot reading pixel coordinates in your ear, you hear a mountain river flowing gently from left to right through a low-pass filter.

turns.speaker: Speaker B
turns.text: That distinction matters. Under the Social Model of Disability, bolting an aria-live distance counter onto a visual grid grants navigational permission, yet leaves blind listeners doing mental trigonometry instead of inhabiting the story.

turns.speaker: Speaker A
turns.text: Drawing on the RNIB and Roundhouse sensory-darkness storytelling collaborations, this small prototype removes the 2D coordinate grid entirely. Every gesture—like pouring out a measure from a stone basin—produces the sound, the voice, and the reflection together.

turns.speaker: Speaker B
turns.text: Still, we have to be honest about what this tiny browser sketch cannot do. Built-in speech synthesis voices remain mechanical compared to a human storyteller, and trading open 2D movement for discrete choices narrows spatial freedom. Yet naming those limits keeps the work grounded.
